title: SAIC buys ISC to bulk up quantum-ready encryption tech
key_facts: Science Applications International Corp. (SAIC) acquired Information Security Corp. (ISC), a developer of cryptographic software, in what executives call a 'tuck-in' buy; terms of the deal, announced Monday (5 Oct 2026), were not disclosed.

ISC's capabilities include public key infrastructure, encryption and credential management software, the cryptographic building blocks that protect the confidentiality, integrity and availability of sensitive data.
ISC builds its products to help customers modernise their cryptographic infrastructure and move to post-quantum cryptography, SAIC said in its announcement.
ISC's CertAgent product has been on the National Security Agency's Commercial Solutions for Classified Components List for more than a decade.
SAIC CEO Jim Reagan said ISC's technologies, joined with SAIC's zero-trust work, give its intelligence and defence customers security and scalability against evolving threats.
All ISC employees and leaders have moved over to SAIC; a company spokeswoman said the focus is on aligning ISC's capabilities within SAIC.
ISC describes its technology as deeply embedded across the US intelligence community and the Defense Department for identity, authentication and data protection.
